Role_Team.positionality: With a PhD in Communications Engineering, 16 years of software development experience, and 12 years of Scrum application in biotechnology as a Product Owner, my background heavily informs my approach to understanding how Scrum practitioners define software quality. This technical and multidisciplinary foundation may lead me to prioritize structural and procedural aspects of software quality over end-user perspectives. Although I consciously strive for objectivity, my extensive experience could unintentionally skew my interpretation toward industry-standard practices and familiar methodologies. Consequently, my positionality may guide me to emphasize empirical rigor and technical accuracy in both data interpretation and the coding process, potentially influencing final research outcomes.

init_codebook.definition: Evaluating quality through the software development process.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions quality at the process level or continuous improvement of processes.
exclusion_criteria: Focuses only on end-product outcomes without mentioning the process.
typical_examples: Quality takes place in the process level and the software level.
atypical_examples: Agile believes in continuous improvement of processes.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Highlights how process improvements contribute to software quality definitions in Scrum.

init_codebook.definition: Quality as defined by conformity to business needs and being defect-free.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions software quality as defect-free or meeting business needs.
exclusion_criteria: Does not mention defect-free or alignment with business needs.
typical_examples: The key attributes are conformity to business needs and free of defects.
atypical_examples: No bugs and meets the business needs.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Defines the outcome expectations of Scrum practitioners regarding software quality.

init_codebook.definition: Quality through code maintainability, readability, and sustainability.
inclusion_criteria: Discusses the maintainability, readability, or sustainability of code.
exclusion_criteria: Only focuses on the end-user product without internal aspects.
typical_examples: We aim for clean code and maintainability.
atypical_examples: Code quality is difficult to define, but necessary.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Explains the internal metrics of quality valued by Scrum practitioners.

init_codebook.definition: The subjective nature of defining quality in software.
inclusion_criteria: Refers to the difficulty or subjectivity in measuring quality.
exclusion_criteria: Provides an objective or specific definition of quality.
typical_examples: Quality is a subjective concept.
atypical_examples: Can be difficult to define, but its absence is noticeable.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Shows the variability in individual interpretations of quality in Scrum practices.

init_codebook.definition: Ongoing process improvements to enhance software quality.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions continuous or ongoing improvement efforts.
exclusion_criteria: Focuses on one-time improvement or no mention of improvement.
typical_examples: Agile process is subject to continuous improvements.
atypical_examples: It's a journey of continuous learning and improvement.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Helps understand how Scrum teams link process improvement with quality outcomes.

Role_Team.positionality: As a Software Developer with a Bachelor's Degree in Information Technology and 30 years in the field, my analytical perspective is heavily influenced by my extensive experience in software development and Scrum methodologies. My industry background positions me to emphasize technical precision and iterative processes when considering how Scrum practitioners define software quality. However, this predisposes me to value structured approaches, leading to biases toward traditional frameworks over creative interpretations. My assumptions may skew towards viewing quality from a process efficiency standpoint. As a result, my positionality will likely guide my coding decisions and data interpretations towards aligning with established IT norms, potentially overlooking nuanced insights.

init_codebook.definition: This code captures the concept of quality derived from the process of development in agile and Scrum methodologies.
inclusion_criteria: Reference to continuous improvement, retrospectives, and processes in agile that enhance quality.
exclusion_criteria: Mentions of only product defects or external quality without reference to process.
typical_examples: The agile process itself is subject to continuous improvements.
atypical_examples: We believe in responding to change over following a plan.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: It highlights how process improvements in Scrum affect the definition and assurance of software quality.

init_codebook.definition: This code represents the view of quality in terms of the finished product being defect-free and meeting user or business needs.
inclusion_criteria: Statements that emphasize end product conformity to requirements and defect-free status.
exclusion_criteria: Discussion solely focused on internal code quality or process without mention of end product.
typical_examples: Software quality is the end result. It has a structural perspective.
atypical_examples: Quality for me is a product meets customer requirements and free of defects.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Demonstrates the emphasis on aligning the software product with business and user expectations as a measure of quality.

init_codebook.definition: Internal Quality refers to aspects of software quality related to the codebase, maintainability, and design flexibility.

exclusion_criteria: Focus solely on external product attributes or defects.
typical_examples: Aims for clean code, maintainable code, and design flexibility.
atypical_examples: Developers write code anyhow. No documentation, no code quality.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Explores how developers view code quality as a crucial component of software quality in Scrum.

init_codebook.definition: This code reflects the complexity and subjectivity involved in defining software quality.
inclusion_criteria: Statements expressing difficulty, subjectivity, or variability in defining quality.
exclusion_criteria: Clear-cut definitions of quality without mention of complexity or subjectivity.
typical_examples: Quality is a subjective concept.
atypical_examples: We can have this argument for days about why you should use certain coding standards.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: It underscores the inherent challenges Scrum practitioners face in articulating a unified definition of software quality.

init_codebook.definition: This code captures the notion of iterative enhancement of processes or code as a pathway to quality.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions of continuous learning, retrospectives, or process adjustments.
exclusion_criteria: Statements about quality without any mention of iterative improvement.
typical_examples: Agile calls for continuous improvement.
atypical_examples: The process becomes more robust when we learn from our mistakes.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: This highlights the role of continuous improvement practices within Scrum as integral to maintaining and defining software quality.

Role_Team.positionality: As a Product Owner with a PhD in Data Science and 30 years in electronic manufacturing, my background deeply grounds my research in both theoretical and practical aspects of software quality. With 7 years of Scrum experience, I approach the question "How Do Scrum Practitioners Define Software Quality?" through a lens that values structured processes and empirical evidence. My extensive industry experience may bias me toward emphasizing quantitative metrics over qualitative insights. These biases may lead me to prioritize data-driven definitions of software quality, potentially overlooking subjective experiences. Thus, my positionality could influence interpretations by skewing data analysis towards technical assessments aligned with my professional and academic training.

init_codebook.definition: Quality involves both the process of development and the final software product.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions quality at process or software level.
Discusses processes assuring quality.
exclusion_criteria: Mentions only end-product quality without process context.
typical_examples: Quality takes place in the process level and the software level.
atypical_examples: Implement and exercise practices that assure quality.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Helps understand how practitioners connect process with software quality.

init_codebook.definition: Software quality is defined by how well it conforms to business needs.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions conformity to business or customer needs as quality.
exclusion_criteria: Mentions technical aspects of quality like code or design without reference to business needs.
typical_examples: Conformity to business needs and free of defects.
atypical_examples: Product confirms to the requirements.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Explores how practitioners prioritize alignment with business needs in quality definitions.

init_codebook.definition: Quality that focuses on code maintainability, understanding, and reusability.
inclusion_criteria: Focus on maintainability, understanding, reuse of code.
exclusion_criteria: Focus only on external attributes like defects.
typical_examples: We also focus on the internal software quality.
atypical_examples: Need a design that is flexible and aims for reusability.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Highlights how internal quality attributes are defined within Scrum practices.

init_codebook.definition: Quality is linked to the process of continuous reflection and improvement.
inclusion_criteria: Emphasizes continuous improvement, retrospectives, or ongoing enhancement of processes.
exclusion_criteria: Mentions singular or static process improvements.
typical_examples: The agile process itself is subject to continuous improvements.
atypical_examples: Experiment to come up with better ways.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Demonstrates the role of continuous improvement in defining software quality.

init_codebook.definition: Acknowledges quality as a subjective concept.
inclusion_criteria: Explicitly states quality is subjective.
Mentions variance in definitions based on viewpoints.
exclusion_criteria: Defines quality purely on objective metrics.
typical_examples: Quality is a subjective concept.
atypical_examples: Different answer from different people.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Illustrates the diverse perspectives Scrum practitioners have on software quality.

init_codebook.definition: Quality is defined by the absence of defects in the software.
inclusion_criteria: Mentions defect-free as a component or definition of quality.
exclusion_criteria: Discusses defects in the context of process improvement only.
typical_examples: Software quality is first and most the product confirms to the requirements and free of defects.
atypical_examples: Software should add value to the business without defects.
init_codebook.relevance_to_RQ: Focuses on the importance of defect elimination in quality definitions by practitioners.

agreements.reason: All roles refer to the importance of the development process in determining software quality. They agree that process improvements, retrospectives, and ongoing reflections enhance software quality, aligning with Agile and Scrum principles.

agreements.code: Product Level Quality / Product Quality / Conformity to Business Needs
agreements.reason: All roles emphasize that software must be defect-free and meet business or customer needs. Although the exact wording differs slightly, the underlying principle of aligning with business requirements and defect-free software is consistent.

All roles focus on code maintainability, readability, and sustainability as key aspects of internal quality. The roles agree that internal code quality is crucial for overall software quality in Scrum practices.

All roles agree on the importance of continuous improvement in processes and practices, as it is a fundamental concept of Agile and Scrum methodologies. They highlight that continuous improvement efforts contribute directly to quality enhancement.

agreements.code: Subjectivity of Quality / Challenges in Defining Quality
agreements.reason: All roles acknowledge the subjective nature of defining software quality. They agree that quality is difficult to measure objectively and often involves variability based on individual interpretations.

disagreements.reason: This code explicitly focuses on defect-free software as a standalone quality metric, which is uniquely emphasized in this role. The other roles combine defect-free status with broader business needs or internal attributes, showing a divergence in emphasis.
